extracted.intended_audience: national patent offices, patent attorneys/agents, applicants, and Contracting States' officials implementing or using the PCT
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural/legal requirements under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) governing international patent applications, national/elected Office interactions, institutional roles, finances, amendments, entry into force, and reservations. Intended to guide Contracting States, Offices, applicants and representatives on permitted actions and obligations under the Treaty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on amendments (no added matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments shall not go beyond the said disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must be limited to what is disclosed in the international application; any other changes that introduce subject-matter beyond the original disclosure are not permitted under the Treaty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments governed by national law for non-provided matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendments shall be in accordance with the national law of the elected State in all respects not provided for in this Treaty and the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the Treaty/Regulations are silent, the elected State's national law governs amendment-related matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of amendments when translation required
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an elected Office requires a translation of the international application, the amendments shall be in the language of the translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a translation into the elected Office's language is required, any amendments for that Office must be in that translation language.

rubrics_metrics.name: No cross‑Office requirement to furnish other Offices' examination papers
rubrics_metrics.description: No elected Office receiving the international preliminary examination report may require that the applicant furnish copies, or information on the contents, of any papers connected with the examination relating to the same international application in any other elected Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An elected Office cannot compel applicants to supply papers or contents from examinations performed by other elected Offices for the same international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of kind of protection per designated State
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may indicate that his international application is for the grant, as far as a designated or elected State is concerned, of an inventor’s certificate, utility certificate, utility model, or other kinds of protection instead of a patent, and the ensuing effect shall be governed by the applicant’s choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For States whose laws provide different kinds of protection, applicants can indicate which specific kind they seek in that State; Article 2(ii) does not apply for purposes of this choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeking two kinds of protection where national law permits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a designated or elected State permits an application to be for the grant of a patent or one kind of protection and also for another of the said kinds, the applicant may indicate the two kinds of protection he is seeking, and the ensuing effect shall be governed by the applicant’s indications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If national law allows dual‑seeking, the applicant’s indication determines effect; Article 2(ii) not applicable for this Article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of regional patent treaties on international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: International applications designating or electing a State party to both a regional patent treaty and the PCT may be filed as applications for such regional patents; national law may provide that designation/election has effect of indicating wish to obtain a regional patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where regional patent treaties exist, PCT applications can serve as regional patent filings when treaty/State law so provides; national law can convert designation/election into an indication for regional patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorrect translation may limit or void patent scope
rubrics_metrics.description: If, because of an incorrect translation of the international application, the scope of any patent granted exceeds the scope of the international application in its original language, competent authorities may retroactively limit the scope of the patent and declare it null and void to the extent it exceeded the original-language scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation errors that enlarge claimed scope relative to the original language allow competent authorities to restrict or invalidate the overbroad parts of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of time limits governed by Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The details for computing time limits referred to in this Treaty are governed by the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Treaty defers specifics of time computation to the Regulations (e.g., how days/months are counted, deadlines falling on non-business days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification of time limits by unanimous decision
rubrics_metrics.description: All time limits fixed in Chapters I and II of this Treaty may, outside any revision under Article 60, be modified by a decision of the Contracting States; such decisions must be unanimous and are made in the Assembly or by correspondence as governed by the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time limits can be changed collectively but require unanimity of Contracting States and adherence to procedural rules in the Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excuse for missed time limits due to mail interruption or unavoidable delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any time limit is not met because of interruption in the mail service or unavoidable loss or delay in the mail, the time limit shall be deemed met in the cases and subject to the proof and other conditions prescribed in the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may be relieved of missed deadlines caused by mail interruptions/loss, but must satisfy proof and conditions set in the Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: State discretion to excuse delay in meeting time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Contracting State shall, as far as that State is concerned, excuse, for reasons admitted under its national law, any delay in meeting any time limit; any Contracting State may also excuse delay for other reasons as it decides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each State can apply its national rules to excuse delays and may choose to excuse other causes at its discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to practice before international authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Any attorney, patent agent, or other person having the right to practice before the national Office with which the international application was filed shall be entitled to practice before the International Bureau and the competent International Searching Authority and competent International Preliminary Examining Authority in respect of that application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualification to practice before the receiving national Office confers entitlement to represent the applicant before the IB, ISA and IPEA for that application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent information services by the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau may furnish information services based on published documents (primarily patents and published applications), either directly or through ISAs or other specialized institutions, with operation particularly facilitating developing countries' acquisition of technical knowledge and technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services can be provided directly or via partners; objective includes assisting developing countries gain access to published know‑how; availability and modes governed by Assembly decisions and agreements with institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and cost rules for information services
rubrics_metrics.description: Information services shall be available to Governments of Contracting States and their nationals and residents; services to Governments shall be furnished at cost, with services to developing country Governments furnished below cost if the difference can be covered from profit on other services or other sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access is broadly available; subsidization for developing-country governments is permitted when funding sources exist; 'cost' means cost above normal national Office/ISA obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly authority over implementation and financing of services
rubrics_metrics.description: Details concerning implementation of information services and financing supplementary to costs shall be governed by decisions of the Assembly and working groups it may set up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly decides operational and financing details and may recommend financing methods and establish working groups to implement them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee for Technical Assistance: establishment and tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assembly shall establish a Committee for Technical Assistance to organize and supervise technical assistance for developing Contracting States in developing their patent systems; tasks include training specialists, loaning experts, and supplying equipment for demonstration/operational purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee composition should regard representation of developing countries; IB shall seek agreements with financing organizations and intergovernmental organizations to fund projects; implementation details decided by the Assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter V provisions not affecting other Chapters' financial provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in Chapter IV (Technical Services) shall affect the financial provisions contained in any other Chapter of this Treaty; such provisions are not applicable to the present Chapter or to its implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial rules in other Chapters remain distinct and are not overridden by technical services provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly composition and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assembly shall consist of the Contracting States; each Contracting State's Government shall be represented by one delegate, who may be assisted by alternates, advisors and experts; a delegate may represent and vote in the name of one State only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each State has one vote; representation is one delegate per State (with assistants) and no delegate may represent multiple States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly powers and functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assembly shall deal with matters concerning maintenance and development of the Union, perform tasks assigned under the Treaty, give directions for revision conferences, review and approve Director General reports and activities, determine program and budget, adopt financial regulations, establish committees and observers, and take other actions to further Union objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed list of duties (i)–(x) enumerates core governance and oversight responsibilities of the Assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly quorum, voting thresholds and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: One-half of the Contracting States shall constitute a quorum; each Contracting State has one vote; in absence of quorum the Assembly may make decisions but they take effect only if quorum and required majority are later attained by correspondence; decisions generally require two‑thirds of votes cast subject to specified provisions; abstentions are not votes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quorum rules, ability to act without quorum subject to later confirmation, and voting majorities (two‑thirds in many cases) govern Assembly decision-making; special rules apply for matters of Chapter II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee composition and election
rubrics_metrics.description: When established the Executive Committee shall consist of States elected by the Assembly from among Assembly members; number of members shall correspond to one‑fourth of Assembly membership (remainders disregarded); elections should regard equitable geographical distribution; members serve from close of session electing them to the close of next ordinary Assembly session and may be re-elected but up to two-thirds maximum of such members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive Committee seat count is formulaic; geographic distribution and term limits are specified; Assembly determines detailed election/re-election rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee functions, meetings and voting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Committee shall prepare the Assembly draft agenda, submit program and budget proposals, submit periodical/ audit reports with comments, ensure execution of the Union program by the Director General, and perform other Treaty-assigned functions; it shall meet once a year in ordinary session and in extraordinary session as convened; voting: one vote per member, decisions by simple majority, quorum is one-half, abstentions not considered votes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive Committee handles preparatory and oversight tasks between Assemblies; procedural rules for meetings and decisions are set out, along with observer admission rules and rule-making authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau duties and Director General role
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative tasks concerning the Union shall be performed by the International Bureau which provides secretariat services; the Director General is chief executive, represents the Union, publishes a Gazette and other publications, and, with designated staff, participates without vote in Assembly, Executive Committee and other committee meetings and acts as ex officio secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IB implements administrative functions; Regulations specify services national Offices must perform to assist IB, ISAs and IPEAs; IB prepares revision conferences and may consult with intergovernmental/non-governmental organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee for Technical Cooperation aims and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assembly shall establish a Committee for Technical Cooperation with composition determined by the Assembly and due regard to equitable representation of developing countries; ISAs and IPEAs are ex officio members; aims include improving services, securing uniformity and uniformly high quality in documentation/working methods of ISAs/IPEAs, and advising on technical problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee may be approached in writing by any Contracting State or interested organization; it can address advice to Director General, Assembly, Executive Committee, ISAs/IPEAs and receiving Offices; procedural details by Assembly decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget financing, fees and contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Union shall have a budget including income and expenses proper to the Union; the budget shall be financed from fees and charges for IB services, sale/royalties on IB publications, gifts/bequests/subventions, rents/interests and other income; amounts of fees/prices should normally cover all IB administration expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a deficit occurs, Contracting States shall pay contributions decided by Assembly with due regard to number of international applications from each; options exist for provisional covering or reimbursing contributions; non-payment may affect voting rights subject to exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working capital fund and headquarters advances
rubrics_metrics.description: The Union shall have a working capital fund constituted by a single payment by each Contracting State; amounts/participation decided by Assembly; where fund insufficient, Assembly shall arrange increases; headquarters State may grant advances under a headquarters agreement and have an ex officio seat while obliged to grant advances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms of payment, increases, reimbursements, and conditions for advances and their denunciation are governed by Assembly decisions and separate agreements with the headquarters State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditing of accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditing of the accounts shall be effected by one or more of the Contracting States or by external auditors, as provided in the financial regulations; they shall be designated, with their agreement, by the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly designates auditors under financial regulations; audit procedures follow those regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations: scope and amendment thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulations annexed to the Treaty provide Rules concerning matters expressly referred to the Regulations by the Treaty, administrative requirements/procedures, and implementation details; the Assembly may amend the Regulations and, subject to paragraph (3), amendments shall require three-fourths of votes cast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain Rules in the Regulations can only be amended by unanimous consent or by non-dissent of Contracting States whose national Office acts as an ISA/IPEA (with special treatment when Authority is an intergovernmental organization); inclusion/exclusion of Rules in specified categories requires specified majorities/consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Instructions by Director General
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulations provide for establishment, under the control of the Assembly, of Administrative Instructions by the Director General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative Instructions implement operational details within the framework of Regulations and are subject to Assembly oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supremacy of Treaty over Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of conflict between provisions of the Treaty and those of the Regulations, the provisions of the Treaty shall prevail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations must conform to Treaty; Treaty provisions govern in case of inconsistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispute settlement by ICJ (subject to reservation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Article 64(5), any dispute between two or more Contracting States concerning interpretation or application of the Treaty or Regulations not settled by negotiation may be brought before the International Court of Justice by any one of the States concerned, unless the States agree another method; the State bringing the dispute shall inform the International Bureau which informs other Contracting States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICJ jurisdiction is available for inter‑State disputes unless a State has made a reservation under Article 64(5); parties may agree alternative settlement methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for Treaty revision and amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Treaty may be revised by special conference (revision conference) called by the Assembly; certain Articles may be amended either by a revision conference or according to Article 61; proposals to amend designated Articles may be initiated by any State member, the Executive Committee, or the Director General and must be communicated six months in advance; adoption requires three‑fourths of votes cast and entry into force requires notifications from three‑quarters of States as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed procedural steps govern initiation, communication timing, voting thresholds, and entry into force; amendments increasing financial obligations bind only States that accept them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becoming party to the Treaty
rubrics_metrics.description: Any State member of the International Union for the Protection of Industrial Property may become party to the Treaty by signature followed by deposit of instrument of ratification, or by deposit of an instrument of accession; instruments are deposited with the Director General and Article 24 of the Stockholm Act applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural formalities for accession/ratification are specified; Stockholm Act provisions apply to relevant matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry into force conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to paragraph (3), the Treaty shall enter into force three months after eight States have deposited instruments of ratification or accession, provided at least four of those States each meet certain application/filing statistical conditions (e.g., >40,000 applications filed, or nationals filed ≥1,000 abroad, or national Office received ≥10,000 foreign applications); 'applications' excludes utility models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry into force requires both a minimum number of ratifications/accessions and statistical participation thresholds to ensure substantive representation; Chapter II applicability has additional prerequisites (three States meeting at least one of the statistical requirements and not declaring non‑application to Chapter II).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservations: opting out of Chapter II and other provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any State may declare it shall not be bound by provisions of Chapter II; other declarations permitted include not being bound by Article 39(1) on furnishing copies/translations, not being bound by delay in national processing preventing publication (subject to limits), declaring international publication not required for that State, declaring that filing outside the State is not equated to an actual filing for prior art purposes (with specified statement of effective date/conditions), or declaring not to consider itself bound by Article 59 (ICJ jurisdiction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reservations must be declared as specified and have binding effects described in the subparagraphs (e.g., affects applicability of Chapter II, Article 39(1), Article 11(3), Article 59); procedural notes (e.g., publication of reservations) made in Editor's Note.
